review_metadata.purpose: Review the three checked-in-safe rendered Decision Work Brief pilots and decide the next product-shape gate.

reviewed_cases.decision_read: Whether the CEO should remove a founding cofounder from operating product leadership while preserving a workable transition, customer continuity, and team clarity.
reviewed_cases.action_consequence_read: The CEO would move product authority first, narrow the cofounder's transition role, and set stop conditions before the conversation instead of running an open-ended cooperation reset.
reviewed_cases.what_lolla_pressed_on_read: The brief says Lolla pressed on authority ambiguity, stop conditions before the conversation, and whether polished role language would hide the missed-delivery problem.
reviewed_cases.uncertainty_read: The starting direction, user intent, vanilla overlap, relationship cost, governance constraints, and lost-value severity remain uncertain.
reviewed_cases.missingness_read: Raw conversation, memo, revised answer, transcript, provider text, and private ledgers are absent from the checked-in artifact.
reviewed_cases.non_claims_read: The brief clearly states it is not correctness proof, not answer-quality measurement, not agent authorization, not human validation, and not proof that clean artifacts mean good advice.
reviewed_cases.readability_read: The decision and action consequence are understandable, but section status lines, backtick field names, and source refs make the surface feel internal.
reviewed_cases.overclaim_risk_read: The concrete authority-first story can feel more validated than the safe source boundary supports.
reviewed_cases.strongest_user_value_signal: A busy CEO can see what would change before the hard conversation: authority transfer, narrowed role, and precommitted stop conditions.
reviewed_cases.strongest_thinness_risk: The artifact cannot verify whether the CEO had already chosen authority transfer or whether relationship/governance costs were decisive.

reviewed_cases.decision_read: Whether to launch a public enterprise beta next month to secure enterprise prospects and extend runway, or instead run a restricted private enterprise proof program.
reviewed_cases.action_consequence_read: The team would stop treating the 900-person logo or public launch as the default path, give both prospects the same paid and scoped private-pilot offer, and award priority to the buyer whose behavior creates usable cash or proof within explicit stop rules.
reviewed_cases.what_lolla_pressed_on_read: The brief says Lolla pressed on whether public launch, logo size, and generic gates were being treated as evidence before buyer behavior, support load, audit-log limits, and stop rules were specified.
reviewed_cases.uncertainty_read: Buyer seriousness, board and investor pressure, launch-risk tolerance, public-page value, starting-direction overlap, and lost-value severity remain uncertain.
reviewed_cases.missingness_read: Raw conversation, raw revised answer, raw memo, provider text, private ledgers, and Product Delta report are absent from the checked-in artifact.
reviewed_cases.non_claims_read: The brief says it does not prove the beta should launch, does not prove private pilot is better advice, does not measure answer quality, does not authorize action, and is not human validated.
reviewed_cases.readability_read: The action story is legible, but source-status vocabulary and evidence references are still too prominent for a polished board/customer reader.
reviewed_cases.overclaim_risk_read: The crisp buyer-behavior action story can make two or three clean cases look like product evidence even though the buyer reality is unverified.
reviewed_cases.strongest_user_value_signal: A busy founder can see how to change the next buyer call: equalize private pilot offers and choose based on evidence-producing behavior rather than logo size.
reviewed_cases.strongest_thinness_risk: The artifact cannot verify whether a public launch had fundraising or recruiting value invisible from checked-in-safe context.

reviewed_cases.decision_read: Whether to deploy an AI-assisted intake routing feature in outpatient clinics next month despite operational, compliance, sales, and staff-capacity constraints.
reviewed_cases.action_consequence_read: The operator would keep the launch narrow but replace the nine-gate checklist with a 48-hour backlog diagnostic, four must-pass operating gates, hard pause triggers, and a sales boundary that validates scheduling and billing routing only.
reviewed_cases.what_lolla_pressed_on_read: The brief says Lolla pressed on whether an exhaustive gate list was becoming a control burden too heavy for exhausted admin staff to operate.
reviewed_cases.uncertainty_read: Actual clinic capacity, compliance acceptance, patient-risk detail, backlog cause, original/revised overlap, and whether compressed gates lost useful controls remain uncertain.
reviewed_cases.missingness_read: Raw conversation, revised answer, memo, live transcript, provider text, and private ledgers are absent from the checked-in artifact.
reviewed_cases.non_claims_read: The brief says it does not prove the routing feature should deploy, does not prove constrained pilot is better advice, does not measure answer quality, does not authorize action, and is not human validated.
reviewed_cases.readability_read: The action consequence is clear, but field labels and source refs still feel like an internal schema render rather than a plain brief.
reviewed_cases.overclaim_risk_read: The clean third example can make the pattern feel more validated than three Codex-assisted checked-in-safe cases support.
reviewed_cases.strongest_user_value_signal: A busy operator can see what changes before go-live: diagnose the backlog cause, compress controls, set hard pause triggers, and narrow the sales claim.
reviewed_cases.strongest_thinness_risk: The artifact cannot verify whether compliance's two-month auditability concern should block even the narrowed pilot.

cross_case_questions.question: Did all three briefs name the decision clearly?
cross_case_questions.rationale: Each brief opens with a recognizable decision: cofounder authority, enterprise beta launch, or assisted intake routing deployment.

cross_case_questions.question: Did all three briefs name a concrete action consequence?
cross_case_questions.rationale: Each brief names what the decision-maker would do differently before a conversation, buyer call, or deployment.

cross_case_questions.question: Did the action consequence differ by decision family rather than reuse generic caution?
cross_case_questions.rationale: The outputs are family-specific: authority transfer, buyer-behavior proof, and operating-control compression.

cross_case_questions.question: Did all three briefs explain what Lolla pressed on in user-useful language?
cross_case_questions.rationale: The pressure reads are useful, but the renderer still wraps them in section status and field-name machinery.

cross_case_questions.question: Did all three preserve uncertainty and non-claims?
cross_case_questions.rationale: All three show high uncertainty, missing private sources, human_validated false, product_proof false, and explicit non-claims.

cross_case_questions.question: Did any brief make clean artifacts feel like proof?
cross_case_questions.rationale: The rendered briefs mitigate overclaim with non-claims, but clean prose plus clear action deltas can still feel like validation.

cross_case_questions.question: Did any brief sound too machinery-flavored for a board/customer reader?
cross_case_questions.rationale: All three carry backtick field names, source-status lines, and source refs in the main reading flow.

cross_case_questions.question: Did checked-in-safe source limits materially weaken the usefulness read?
cross_case_questions.rationale: The action-consequence signal is useful, but starting direction, private nuance, original/revised overlap, user intent, and lost value remain unverified.

cross_case_questions.question: Is the brief useful because it explains decision work, not because it displays internal machinery?
cross_case_questions.rationale: The useful part is the decision/action story; the machinery is currently too visible and should be moved out of the main body.

cross_case_questions.question: What would a busy decision-maker understand from these three briefs that they would not get from the final revised answer alone?
cross_case_questions.answer: They would see the before/after action consequence, what pressure changed the action, what remains uncertain, and what the audit must not claim.
cross_case_questions.rationale: The brief adds process meaning and limits around the revised answer rather than only presenting the recommendation.

cross_case_observations.common_useful_pattern: All three briefs make the action consequence visible before the evidence appendix dominates.
cross_case_observations.common_uncertainty_pattern: All three depend on checked-in-safe artifacts that omit raw conversation, revised answer, memo, provider text, and private ledgers.
cross_case_observations.common_language_pattern: All three render enough internal field labels and source-status language to feel like product-shape artifacts rather than customer-ready briefs.
cross_case_observations.common_overclaim_pattern: As the action story gets clearer, the non-human and source-limited status must become easier, not harder, for readers to notice.
cross_case_observations.why_not_more_cases_yet: More cases would add evidence volume but would not fix the current language problem.
cross_case_observations.why_not_runtime_yet: The artifacts are provisional, checked-in-safe, non-human-validated, and still too machinery-flavored for runtime presentation.

action_consequence_pattern.summary: The strongest cross-case signal is that the Decision Work Brief consistently answers what would be done differently now.

case_specific_actions.action_consequence: Move product authority first, narrow transition support, and set stop conditions before the conversation.
Use equal paid/scoped private pilot offers and choose based on proof-producing buyer behavior before any public launch.
Run a backlog diagnostic, compress controls, define hard pause triggers, and narrow the pilot's sales meaning.

uncertainty_pattern.summary: All three briefs preserve uncertainty, but the cues are too metadata-shaped for a non-technical reader.
recurring_uncertainties: stakeholder, legal, governance, compliance, buyer, or patient-risk context

source_context_pattern.summary: Checked-in-safe context is enough to test the brief shape, but not enough to verify final customer-facing interpretation.
source_context_pattern.reason_not_next: The immediate blocker visible across all three examples is language and presentation, not absence of enough cases to notice the shape.

language_and_readability_pattern.summary: The brief body answers useful user questions, but the renderer still exposes schema-like keys, status vocabulary, and source refs in the main flow.
examples_of_language_risk: backtick field labels such as action_consequence and decision_story_read
status and source-status lines before each story section
source refs dominating attention before the reader has absorbed the decision story
language_and_readability_pattern.recommended_repair: Patch the renderer toward plain-language headings and move source/custody detail into a compact Evidence and Limits appendix.

overclaim_risk_pattern.summary: Non-claims are present, but polished action prose can still imply more validation than exists.
overclaim_risk_pattern.strongest_overclaim_risk: Three clean rendered briefs can look like product evidence even though all are Codex-assisted, non-human-validated, and source-limited.
mitigations_that_worked: what was not proven renders in every brief
overclaim_risk_pattern.remaining_problem: The non-claims are visible but feel appended rather than integrated into the reader's confidence calibration.

product_usefulness_read.strongest_useful_signal: Across three different decision families, the brief consistently clarifies action consequence.
product_usefulness_read.strongest_missingness_thinness_risk: The checked-in-safe surface cannot verify private context, original/revised overlap, user intent, lost value, buyer reality, compliance tolerance, or governance constraints.
product_usefulness_read.strongest_overclaim_risk: Clean prose can make provisional Codex-assisted interpretation feel more validated than it is.
product_usefulness_read.strongest_product_language_risk: The current renderer still reads like a structured artifact dump in places, especially through field labels, source refs, and status vocabulary.
product_usefulness_read.strongest_reason_not_to_integrate_runtim: The brief is not plain-language enough, not human validated, and not local-private adequacy checked.

decision_gate.rationale: The three-case pattern is useful because it consistently names action consequence, but the rendered language is too field-label-heavy and machinery-flavored for a board/customer reader.
decision_gate.why_not_five_case_batch: More cases would not fix the current language problem, and expansion before a renderer patch would multiply internal-looking examples.
decision_gate.why_not_local_private_adequacy_check_nex: Local-private adequacy remains important, but the checked-in examples already reveal a surface-language blocker that can be fixed before deeper source review.
decision_gate.why_not_pause_or_stop: The brief format is useful enough to repair rather than pause or simplify away.

next_recommendation.recommended_next_pr: PR123 Decision Work Brief Plain-Language Renderer Patch v0
next_recommendation.recommended_action: Patch the renderer so the main body reads as a plain-language decision brief, with source refs, statuses, and custody details moved into a compact Evidence and Limits appendix.
do_not_do_next: Do not create a five-case batch before patching language.
Do not remove uncertainty or non-claims.
Do not hide source status entirely.
Do not treat three cases as product proof.
